name: entropy of aabb is one bit
ref: hand-computed: p = 1/2 for a and b, H = 2 * (1/2) * 1 = 1

name: entropy of abcd is two bits
ref: hand-computed: four equal p = 1/4, H = 4 * (1/4) * 2 = 2

example.title: Four distinct bytes, each seen once, give two bits
example.note: Two bits is the number of bits needed to label four different things.

name: entropy of abcdefgh is three bits
ref: hand-computed: eight equal p = 1/8, H = 8 * (1/8) * 3 = 3

name: entropy of one repeated byte is +0, not -0
ref: hand-computed: p = 1 for a, the term is 1 * (0 - log2 1) = +0

name: entropy of empty input is 0
ref: hand-computed: no byte has a non-zero count, the sum is 0.0

name: entropy of all 256 byte values is eight bits
ref: hand-computed: 256 equal p = 1/256, H = 256 * (1/256) * 8 = 8

example.title: All 256 byte values give the maximum of eight bits
example.note: Every byte value appears once, so the bytes are spread evenly, and eight bits per byte is the most possible.

name: entropy of non-ASCII input (é is two bytes)
ref: hand-computed: c3 and a9 once each, H = 2 * (1/2) * 1 = 1

name: entropy of binary input
ref: hand-computed: 00 and ff twice each in four bytes, H = 1

name: frequency of aabb
ref: hand-computed: a 2 of 4 (50 percent), b 2 of 4 (50 percent), tie ordered by byte

name: frequency sorts by count descending
ref: hand-computed: a 3 of 4 (75 percent), b 1 of 4 (25 percent)

example.title: The most common byte comes first
example.note: Bytes are written as numbers, so 97 is the letter a. The list is sorted by count, highest first.

name: frequency of a tie in count orders by byte
ref: hand-computed: b before a is still ordered 97 then 98, each 1 of 2 (50 percent)

name: frequency of empty input is an empty list
ref: hand-computed: no byte value is present

name: frequency of non-ASCII input (bytes c3 and a9)
ref: hand-computed: 169 (a9) and 195 (c3), each 1 of 2 (50 percent), tie ordered by byte

example.title: Non-ASCII text is counted in bytes, not letters
example.note: The letter é is two bytes in UTF-8 (195 and 169), so each one is counted separately.

name: frequency of binary input
ref: hand-computed: 00 twice (50 percent), 80 once (25 percent), ff once (25 percent)
